newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Ascom reshuffles Timeplex, partner sought.
newsitem.headline: Ascom reshuffles Timeplex, partner sought.

text.p: Swiss telecommunications group Ascom Holding AG said it had cut 270 jobs as part of a sweeping restructuring of its Ascom Timeplex Inc. unit as it continues the search for a cooperation partner.

Chief financial officer Jakob Schlapbach told reporters that negotiations with a partner for Timeplex collapsed during the summer, when the potential partner encountered profitability problems and withdrew from the talks.

Talks were now underway with new candidates and Schlapback said Ascom was still open to a wide range of possibilities, including an outright sale of Timeplex or a majority or minority stake by another company.
Timeplex has long been a problem child for Ascom, which bought the New Jersey-based company in 1991.
Timeplex, a leader in the area of enterprise networks, forms the core of Ascom's Enterprise Network segment, which recorded a loss of 39 million Swiss francs in the first half of 1996.
Following the collapse of the talks, which had moved into the stage of exclusivity, Ascom decided to restructure Timeplex.
In addition to cutting 270 jobs, about one-fifth of Timeplex' personnel, a new management team has been installed and Timeplex has focused its product strategy on Wide Area Networks (WAN).
Job cuts were completed by the end of September and Ascom took restructuring costs and provisions in the first half, pushing extraordinary items into a loss of 15 million francs.

While the break-down of the talks are another setback for Timeplex, Schlapbach said Ascom did not have to return to the drawing board as the due diligence process had now been completed, a process that would have to be done in any case.
Timeplex is currently trying to make up for a delayed launch of its Synchrony range of products, which has won positive feedback from customers and an increasing order book.
However, Ascom admits that it lost customers due to the delayed launch and it is an uphill battle to win them back.
